Hyundai Unveils i30 Sedan N Monochrome Because Customers Wanted a Toned-Down Look
16 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Hyundai has officially unveiled the Hyundai i30 Sedan N Monochrome. The special limited-edition version of the performance sedan moves away from the vibrant trim accents, going instead for a dark, minimalist, and stripped-back look. Only 200 lucky customers will be able to get their hands on the stealthy Hyundai sedan.
Understated yet undeniable. This is how Hyundai makes a long story short with the all-new i30 Sedan N Monochrome as the lead actor, but one that doesn’t seem to like the spotlight very much. The automaker says it listened to customers who wanted a toned-down and more mature look, and this is what it is giving them now.
Gone is the striking red trim that the standard i30 Sedan N comes with. It has been replaced with body-colored paint for a uniform look. The front bumper inlays, side sills, rear diffuser, and brake calipers are finished entirely in black rather than the usual standout color.
The special edition Hyundai i30 N gains unpainted carbon-fiber mirror caps and a redesigned carbon fiber rear wing spoiler and rides on newly designed 19-inch forged alloy wheels, which are finished in matte black.
Photo: Hyundai Customers can go for one of the two exterior paint options available for the performance sedan: Abyss Black Pearl for a fully blacked-out, murdered-out look, or Performance Blue, which retains the darkened trim pieces.
The Monochrome is the only variant in the entire i30 Sedan N lineup to feature the premium Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel and a matching gear shifter boot. The buttons on the steering wheel have been changed to black to fit the single-tone cockpit. The only color accent on board is the stitching in Performance Blue.
The underpinnings remain identical to the standard model, which means that the car still delivers true track-ready performance. The 2.0-liter turbocharged engine generates 276 horsepower (280 metric horsepower) and 289 pound-feet (392 Newton meters) of torque.
The sedan still rockets from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.8 seconds when equipped with the dual-clutch automatic transmission and Launch Control or 5.4 seconds when the six-speed manual transmission is involved.
Photo: Hyundai The all-new Hyundai i30 Sedan N Monochrome will arrive in Australian showrooms starting in November 2026. Only 200 such units will see the light of day with both manual and automatic transmissions.
The official pricing will depend on the market and has yet to be revealed, but it will surely come with a premium over the starting price of the i30 Sedan N standard model, which starts at 53,500 Australian dollars (US $37,316).
Hyundai has plans to launch the performance sedan with restrained looks in Canada, Korea (in late October), and of course, Australia, but its arrival in the United States hasn’t been officially confirmed.
